diagnostic_evidence.quote: AFF-Fair-SMW achieved fairness levels comparable to existing baselines while offering substantial runtime advantages.
However, Figure \ref{fg - GermanRunTime} reveals that AFF-Fair-SMW incurred the highest overall runtime, while the remaining algorithms exhibited similar performance.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract claims a twice-as-fast runtime improvement and twice as much balance, but the paper's own conclusion only claims comparable balance, and the German experiment reports AFF-Fair-SMW as the slowest overall. The advertised balance and universal runtime advantages are not supported by the reported results.

failure_location.quote: We achieve an improvement in computation time that is twice as fast as the state-of-the-art, and also flexible enough to achieve twice as much balance.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Revise the abstract to claim only the supported comparable balance and dataset-dependent runtime improvements.
issues.overall_effect: Overstates the method's empirical fairness and runtime guarantees.
issues.title: Abstract overclaims twice the balance and universal speedup
issues.why_classification: The repair is prose-only, but it withdraws an advertised guarantee (twice the balance), so it is more than a local typo.

issues.failure_explanation: The equivalence requires H_{i\ell} to be a 0/1 cluster indicator and the column sum to equal the cluster size. But H is the orthonormal spectral embedding, so f_i H_{i\ell} need not count intersections and sum_i H_{i\ell} need not equal |C_\ell|. Thus F^T H=0 is not equivalent to exact group balance.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the lemma for a discrete indicator matrix H, and separately state that F^T H=0 is only a spectral relaxation for the orthonormal embedding.
issues.overall_effect: The fairness constraint F^T H=0 and the optimization problem mainobj are not justified as exact fairness constraints; at best they are a relaxation.
issues.title: Fairness equivalence lemma treats embedding H as a cluster indicator
issues.why_classification: The central formal claim that the linear constraint enforces group balance fails; the paper's fairness guarantee would need to be weakened to a relaxation.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $Z \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times (n-h+1)}$ denote an orthonormal basis for the null space of $F^T$.
Notice that \eqref{SMW2} is equivalent to \eqref{SMW1} in the sense that the maximizer $H$ is the same.

issues.failure_explanation: Z is a rectangular orthonormal basis, so Z^T Z=I but Z is not invertible and Z^T is not Z^{-1}. Moreover (Z^T G Z)^{-1} is not generally Z^T G^{-1} Z. Therefore the claimed equivalence between the constrained maximization with G and the constrained minimization with G^{-1} is invalid.

failure_location.quote: using the fact that $Z^T=Z^{-1}$ we can reformulate this problem as follows

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, re-derive the constrained optimization without using Z^{-1} and establish the correct equivalence or use a correct generalized eigenvalue formulation.
issues.overall_effect: The Fair-SMW reformulation is not justified; the algorithm may solve a different optimization problem than the stated fair spectral clustering problem.
issues.title: SMW derivation uses a false inverse identity for rectangular Z
issues.why_classification: The root derivation of the entire Fair-SMW method is invalid, so the central algorithmic formulation loses its theoretical basis.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \min_{H} \left( \frac{1}{2}\text{Tr}(H^T G^{-1} H) - \frac{\mu}{2} \text{Tr}(H^T F F^T H) \right) = \min_{H} \frac{1}{2}\text{Tr}\left(H^T \left( G^{-1} - \mu F F^T \right) H \right)

issues.failure_explanation: The reduced subproblem from the stated augmented Lagrangian has matrix G^{-1}-\mu FF^T, but the next labelled problem uses G^{-1}+\mu FF^T. The plus sign is not derived and changes the matrix whose inverse is used in the SMW identity.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a consistent augmented Lagrangian sign (standard plus penalty) and update the gradient and block system accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The derivation of the matrix inverted by SMW is inconsistent with the stated Lagrangian, so the SMW step is not justified as written.
issues.title: Sign flip in augmented Lagrangian derivation of SMW3
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and the intended plus-sign matrix is clear from the subsequent SMW formula.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \State Construct the fairness-adjusted matrix $U_{\text{sym}} = G_{\mathrm{sym}} - M (F^T M)^{-1} F^T G_{\mathrm{sym}}$

issues.failure_explanation: With M=G^{-1}F the algorithm forms G - G^{-1}F(F^T G^{-1}F)^{-1}F^T G, whereas the derived SMW matrix is G - G F(F^T G F)^{-1}F^T G. The algorithm therefore does not implement the stated Fair-SMW construction.

failure_location.quote: \State Compute the projection matrix $M = G_{\mathrm{sym}}^{-1} F$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace M=G_{\mathrm{sym}}^{-1}F by M=G_{\mathrm{sym}}F (or equivalently use the displayed U expression with F^T G_{\mathrm{sym}} F).
issues.overall_effect: The executable algorithm alg:smw-cluster is not the Fair-SMW method derived in the paper.
issues.title: Fair-SMW algorithm computes wrong matrix in projection step
issues.why_classification: The error is a one-line correction in the algorithm and the intended construction is visible from the preceding definition.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds the numerical range of the non-symmetric matrix D^{-1}W by its spectral radius, which is invalid. For a star graph with 16 vertices, the symmetric part of G_rw has a negative eigenvalue below -2, so x^T G_rw x can be negative. Thus G_rw is not generalized positive definite.

failure_location.quote: $G_{rw}$ has real eigenvalues and is generalized positive definite. That is $\bm{x}^T G_{rw}\bm{x} >0$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a different shift or restrict to graphs for which the symmetric part of G_rw is positive definite; this changes the RW variant.
issues.overall_effect: The positivity assumption needed for the RW variant and the SMW inversion is false, so the RW-Fair-SMW variant lacks its stated justification.
issues.title: G_rw is not generalized positive definite
issues.why_classification: The theorem is false and the advertised RW variant may fail its positivity/invertibility hypothesis.

issues.failure_explanation: The identity used to simplify the projection is false for general F and D. For example, with F=(1,-1)^T and D=diag(1,2), the left side is [1,-1/2] while the right side is [0.75,-0.75]. Thus the subsequent symmetry argument for U_rw does not follow.

failure_location.quote: The eigenvalues of $U_{\text{rw}} = G_{\text{rw}}(I-F(F^T G_{\text{rw}}F)^{-1}F^T G_{\text{rw}})$ are real.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide a correct proof of realness or restrict the theorem to cases where the identity holds.
issues.overall_effect: The real-eigenvalue claim for the RW variant is left unsupported by the given proof.
issues.title: Proof of real eigenvalues for U_rw uses false identity
issues.why_classification: The proof has a false nontrivial identity; repairing it requires a new argument, but the statement itself is not shown false.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof starts from the wrong expression for U (the inverse of G+\mu FF^T rather than the SMW inverse or its limit). More importantly, A_sym F=0 does not imply G_rw F=2F or G_aff F=nF, so the claimed similar simplification for G_rw and G_aff is false in general.

failure_location.quote: A similar statement holds for $G_{\textup{rw}}$ and $G_{\textup{aff}}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the first line of the proof and restrict the theorem to G_sym, or add appropriate hypotheses for the other variants.
issues.overall_effect: The appendix result does not correctly justify the G_sym simplification and its extension to the other G variants is unsupported.
issues.title: Appendix theorem misstates U and extends simplification incorrectly
issues.why_classification: The G_sym part is locally repairable, but the stated extension to two other variants is false and must be removed or rehypothesized.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes only the upper bound ≤2. Equality can fail, for example for non-bipartite graphs whose largest normalized Laplacian eigenvalue is strictly less than 2. Thus the stated supremum equality is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the equality by the upper bound sup ≤ 2 or state that the quadratic form is bounded by 2.
issues.overall_effect: Only the upper bound is used elsewhere, so the downstream eigenvalue interval arguments are not invalidated; the equality claim itself is false.
issues.title: Theorem states equality 2 for normalized Laplacian supremum but proof only gives upper bound
issues.why_classification: A short local correction restores a true statement and no substantive downstream claim depends on the false equality.
